dedupe_keys.name: nos villes vertes urban vegetation maps and statistics for french communes kermap

description: Nos Villes Vertes is a free platform that maps urban vegetation and gives statistics such as tree canopy cover, herbaceous cover, canopy per inhabitant and tree carbon storage potential for every town in France, with rankings between cities. Kermap, a French geospatial company, launched it in 2019 and refreshed it in July 2023 with new aerial photographs that IGN releases as open data, on which its artificial intelligence models detect and extract vegetation automatically; the update added herbaceous cover and new rankings. Coverage is all French communes, including overseas cities such as Fort-de-France. Format and access: public web maps and figures; finer data consolidated by photo-interpretation at any scale (region, intercommunality, IRIS) are sold as Kermap services with analyses of cooling, noise, runoff and carbon. Licence: free to view, no licence stated; detailed data are commercial. Caveats: platform values come from automated detection without human checks. It supports urban heat and green infrastructure planning. Related catalogue records are the USDA Forest Service tree canopy cover and the Copernicus Urban Atlas street tree layer.
